simple_definition: In addition; used to introduce a further point.
detailed_definition: In addition; besides; used to introduce a statement that adds to or supports the previous one.
examples: The plan is expensive. Furthermore, it is unlikely to solve the underlying problem.
Furthermore, research shows that exercise improves mental health.
ielts_relevance: Essential linking word for adding points in Task 2 body paragraphs.

simple_definition: Used to introduce an additional point or fact.
detailed_definition: As a further matter; besides; used to introduce a statement that supports or adds to a previous one.
examples: The policy is unpopular. Moreover, it has failed to reduce emissions.
Moreover, the new system will save the company a significant amount of money.
ielts_relevance: Common formal linking word, interchangeable with furthermore.

simple_definition: In spite of that; even so.
detailed_definition: In spite of what has just been said or referred to; even so; notwithstanding.
examples: The journey was long and tiring. Nevertheless, they arrived on time.
Critics disliked the film; nevertheless, it was a huge box office success.
ielts_relevance: Common contrast linker for acknowledging counterpoints in Task 2.

simple_definition: In spite of that; nevertheless.
detailed_definition: Despite what has just been said; nevertheless.
examples: The risks are significant; nonetheless, many believe the benefits outweigh them.
It was a small gesture, but a meaningful one nonetheless.
ielts_relevance: Interchangeable with nevertheless for high-band contrast linking.

simple_definition: Used to compare or contrast two facts.
detailed_definition: In contrast or comparison with the fact that; while on the contrary.
examples: In rural areas, farming is the main occupation, whereas in cities, most people work in offices.
She prefers quiet evenings at home, whereas her husband loves going out.
ielts_relevance: Essential for comparison essays and describing contrasting data.

simple_definition: Introducing a fact or idea that is the opposite of what has just been stated.
detailed_definition: In a way that is opposite or contrary to something just stated.
examples: Wealthier nations tend to have lower birth rates. Conversely, developing countries often see higher rates.
Some argue technology isolates people; conversely, others believe it brings them closer together.
ielts_relevance: High-band linking word for presenting opposing viewpoints.

simple_definition: Although; even though.
detailed_definition: Although; used to introduce a factor that slightly reduces the force of what has just been said.
examples: The plan was approved, albeit with several reservations from the committee.
Sales improved, albeit slowly, over the following months.
ielts_relevance: High-band concession word used mid-sentence for nuance.

simple_definition: Used to say that a statement is probably true or can be argued.
detailed_definition: It can be argued or shown that; used to soften or support a claim.
examples: This is arguably one of the most important inventions of the century.
Social media is arguably the most influential form of media today.
ielts_relevance: Useful hedging adverb for stating a strong but debatable opinion.

simple_definition: Without doubt; certainly.
detailed_definition: It is not disputed or doubted that; certainly.
examples: The internet has undoubtedly transformed the way we communicate.
This is undoubtedly one of the biggest challenges facing the industry today.
ielts_relevance: Common adverb for stating strong certainty in essays.

simple_definition: Used to say that something is likely to be true.
detailed_definition: Used to convey that what is stated is very likely, though not known for certain.
examples: Presumably, the company will need to raise prices to cover the extra costs.
She didn't attend the meeting, presumably because she was ill.
ielts_relevance: Useful hedging adverb for speculative reasoning.

simple_definition: Appearing to be a certain way, but perhaps not really.
detailed_definition: As far as one knows or can tell; giving the impression of being something, without necessarily being so.
examples: Despite the seemingly simple solution, the problem persisted for years.
He remained seemingly calm throughout the entire interview.
ielts_relevance: Useful for expressing appearance versus reality in essays.

simple_definition: As is certain to happen; unavoidably.
detailed_definition: In a way that is certain to happen and cannot be avoided.
examples: As cities grow, traffic congestion will inevitably increase.
Mistakes are inevitably made when a task is rushed.
ielts_relevance: Common for describing unavoidable consequences in Task 2.

simple_definition: In a way that is a permanent, essential part of something.
urdu_meaning: فطری طور پر، بنیادی طور پر
detailed_definition: In a way that exists as a natural or basic part of something.
examples: Some argue that competition is inherently beneficial to economic growth.
Not all risk is inherently bad; some risks lead to great rewards.
ielts_relevance: Useful for essays discussing the fundamental nature of a topic.

simple_definition: In a basic or essential way.
detailed_definition: In a central or primary manner; concerning the basic nature of something.
examples: The two systems are fundamentally different in how they approach education.
I fundamentally disagree with the idea that punishment alone reduces crime.
ielts_relevance: Common adverb for stating a core opinion or comparison.

simple_definition: In a way that only relates to the surface, not deeply.
detailed_definition: In a way that appears true or real at first, but is not so when examined more deeply.
examples: Superficially, the two proposals seem very similar, but their long-term effects differ greatly.
The report only superficially addressed the root causes of the problem.
ielts_relevance: Useful for pointing out surface-level versus deeper analysis.

simple_definition: Clearly, based on the evidence available.
detailed_definition: As is clear from the evidence available; clearly, obviously.
examples: Evidently, the new policy has not achieved its intended goals.
She was evidently exhausted after the long journey.
ielts_relevance: Common transitional adverb for introducing an observation.

simple_definition: After something else has happened; afterward.
detailed_definition: Occurring after or as a result of something else; afterward.
examples: The company launched the product and subsequently saw a sharp rise in sales.
He was fined for speeding and subsequently lost his driving license.
ielts_relevance: Common time-sequence adverb useful in narrative Task 1 process descriptions.

simple_definition: As a result; therefore.
detailed_definition: As a result of a particular action or set of circumstances; therefore.
examples: Fuel prices rose sharply; consequently, transport costs increased across the board.
She missed the deadline and consequently lost the contract.
ielts_relevance: Extremely common cause-effect linker for Task 2.

simple_definition: By that means; as a result of that.
urdu_meaning: اس طرح سے، جس کے باعث
detailed_definition: By that means; as a result of that action.
examples: The new law reduces paperwork, thereby saving businesses valuable time.
She studied every night, thereby improving her grades significantly.
ielts_relevance: Useful for linking a cause directly to its effect within one sentence.

simple_definition: By which; through which.
detailed_definition: By which; through which a particular method or process happens.
examples: The council introduced a scheme whereby residents can recycle household waste for free.
They developed a system whereby employees could report problems anonymously.
ielts_relevance: Formal relative adverb useful for describing processes and systems.

simple_definition: In spite of; without being affected by.
detailed_definition: In spite of; despite something, without being prevented by it.
examples: Notwithstanding the criticism, the government proceeded with the reform.
The project was completed on time, notwithstanding several major setbacks.
ielts_relevance: Formal high-band alternative to 'despite'.

simple_definition: Considering; taking into account.
detailed_definition: Taking a particular fact or circumstance into consideration; because of.
examples: In light of recent events, the school has updated its safety procedures.
In light of the evidence, the jury reached a different conclusion.
ielts_relevance: Useful formal phrase for introducing reasoning based on evidence.

simple_definition: Concerning; in relation to.
detailed_definition: Concerning; in connection with a particular subject.
examples: With regard to the budget, several changes have been proposed.
There is ongoing debate with regard to the ethics of animal testing.
ielts_relevance: Common formal phrase to introduce or narrow a topic.

simple_definition: Considering everything; in general.
detailed_definition: Taking everything into account; in general, considering everything.
examples: On the whole, the trial was considered a success.
On the whole, people are living longer and healthier lives than in the past.
ielts_relevance: Common summarizing phrase for Task 2 conclusions.

simple_definition: In general; mostly.
detailed_definition: On the whole; in general, considering everything.
examples: By and large, the reforms have been well received by the public.
By and large, students performed better this year than last.
ielts_relevance: Common idiomatic phrase for general statements in Speaking.

simple_definition: Mostly; in large part.
detailed_definition: Mostly; largely, used to qualify the degree of agreement or truth in a statement.
examples: To a large extent, a person's success depends on their upbringing.
I agree, to a large extent, with the argument presented in the article.
ielts_relevance: Essential hedging phrase for partial-agreement Task 2 essays.

simple_definition: Mainly; for the most part.
detailed_definition: For the most part; mainly; to the greatest extent.
examples: The workforce in this sector is predominantly female.
The economy is predominantly based on agriculture and tourism.
ielts_relevance: Common for describing the main composition of a group in Task 1.

simple_definition: Noticeably; to an obvious degree.
detailed_definition: Noticeably; clearly, to an extent that is easily seen.
examples: Life expectancy has markedly improved over the past fifty years.
The two approaches differ markedly in their overall cost.
ielts_relevance: Common intensifying adverb for Task 1 comparisons.

simple_definition: To a very small degree; slightly.
detailed_definition: To a very small degree; slightly.
examples: Sales increased only marginally compared to the previous quarter.
The revised plan is marginally better than the original one.
ielts_relevance: Opposite of 'markedly' — useful for small changes in Task 1.

simple_definition: In a way that is sudden and striking; very much.
detailed_definition: In a sudden and striking manner; to a great extent.
examples: The cost of solar panels has dropped dramatically over the past decade.
Public opinion shifted dramatically after the scandal broke.
ielts_relevance: Common intensifying adverb for Task 1 sharp trend changes.

simple_definition: To a great or significant extent.
detailed_definition: To a great or significant extent; considerably.
examples: The number of applicants has increased substantially since last year.
Reducing waste could substantially lower the company's operating costs.
ielts_relevance: Common intensifier for describing large changes in Task 1.

simple_definition: In a way that happens gradually, step by step.
detailed_definition: In a way that continues gradually or step by step, becoming greater or more advanced.
examples: The company has progressively expanded its operations into new markets.
Regulations have become progressively stricter over the last decade.
ielts_relevance: Useful adverb for describing continuous gradual trends.

simple_definition: Always; in every case, without exception.
detailed_definition: In every case or on every occasion; always.
examples: Traffic invariably gets worse during the holiday season.
She invariably arrives early for every meeting.
ielts_relevance: Formal way to say 'always' in academic writing.

simple_definition: On purpose; intentionally.
detailed_definition: Consciously and intentionally; on purpose.
examples: The company deliberately kept prices low to attract new customers.
He deliberately avoided answering the difficult question.
ielts_relevance: Common adverb for describing intentional actions or policy choices.

simple_definition: Without intention; by accident.
detailed_definition: Without intention; accidentally, as a result of carelessness.
examples: The new policy may inadvertently discourage small businesses from hiring.
She inadvertently deleted an important file while cleaning up her desktop.
ielts_relevance: Opposite of 'deliberately' — useful for unintended consequences.

simple_definition: Open to disagreement; not certain.
detailed_definition: Able to be argued about; not proven or certain, therefore open to debate.
examples: It is arguable whether social media does more harm than good.
The success of the policy remains arguable, given the mixed results.
ielts_relevance: Useful for presenting a balanced, debatable viewpoint.

simple_definition: Unable to be questioned or doubted; certainly true.
detailed_definition: Unable to be challenged or denied; certainly true.
examples: It is indisputable that access to clean water saves lives.
The evidence for climate change is now considered indisputable by most scientists.
ielts_relevance: Strong adjective for stating facts with full certainty.

simple_definition: Seeming reasonable or probable.
detailed_definition: Seeming reasonable or probable; believable.
examples: The most plausible explanation for the delay is a technical fault.
Her excuse sounded plausible, but nobody quite believed it.
ielts_relevance: Useful adjective for evaluating explanations and causes.

simple_definition: Causing or likely to cause disagreement.
detailed_definition: Causing or likely to cause an argument; controversial.
examples: Immigration remains one of the most contentious political issues today.
The proposed changes to the law proved highly contentious.
ielts_relevance: Formal synonym for 'controversial' in higher-band essays.
